enzyme_name: none identified (hydrolysis half-step of amine-oxidase deamination of tyramine)
organism_context: MetaCyc RXN-15197; the imine substrate arises from copper/flavin amine oxidase action on tyramine
rationale: MetaCyc splits oxidative deamination of tyramine into Schiff-base formation and hydrolysis of the free 4-(2-iminoethyl)phenol to 4-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde + ammonia; no protein is assigned to this hydrolysis half, which proceeds without a catalyst in water. I could not identify a catalysing enzyme, so 'unknown' rather than a guessed monofunctional call.
direction_note: Imine hydrolysis in bulk water is effectively one-way at physiological ammonia levels; ModelSEED's reverse-only call would require 4-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde to condense with NH3 in vivo.

organism_context: Selenocysteine GPx1-GPx4 in mammals; Cys-type homologues (E. coli BtuE, plant GPXs) in bacteria and plants
rationale: Glutathione peroxidase has a single peroxidatic Sec/Cys active site and no second catalytic activity; GPx4's structural role in the sperm mitochondrial capsule is moonlighting and is excluded by protocol. Called from established enzymology, no search needed.
direction_note: GSSG, the entire oxidised half of the couple, is missing (status MI matches C20H32N6O12S2 exactly), so both estimators scored the non-reaction 'water -> hydrogen peroxide' and inverted the arrow; the real peroxidatic reduction is irreversible forward.

organism_context: Human CHKA/CHKB, yeast CKI1, Streptococcus pneumoniae LicA, plant CK
rationale: Choline kinase is a single-domain small-molecule kinase; its ability to also phosphorylate ethanolamine is broadened substrate specificity on the same phosphotransfer chemistry, not a second catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional. Called from established enzymology.
direction_note: Phosphocholine (C5H13NO4P) is missing from the products, leaving 'ATP -> ADP + H+'; the real ATP-dependent phosphorylation is physiologically irreversible forward, so ModelSEED's reverse call is an artefact of the broken equation.

organism_context: MetaCyc RXN-14497; no EC number and no protein assigned
rationale: A GSH-mediated disulfide reduction with no enzyme attached; such exchanges run spontaneously or are accelerated by glutaredoxins, and I found no characterised GSH-dependent D-cystine reductase. GSSG is missing from the products (status MI matches C20H32N6O12S2).
direction_note: Restoring GSSG makes this a near-isoenergetic thiol-disulfide exchange whose direction is set by the cellular GSH/GSSG ratio rather than by any enzyme, so neither a forward-only nor a reverse-only bound is defensible.

organism_context: Camellia sinensis (tea) leaf; releases aroma aglycones such as eugenol during oolong/black tea manufacture
rationale: The tea GH1 diglycosidase beta-primeverosidase hydrolyses the intact beta-primeveroside off aroma aglycones in one step; substrate-specificity work and crystal structures show a single glycoside-hydrolase active site and no second catalytic activity.
direction_note: A retaining glycosidase cannot condense free eugenol with free primeverose in water, so ModelSEED's reverse-only assignment has no enzymatic counterpart.

organism_context: E. coli YqjG, yeast Ecm4/Gto, Sphingobium PcpF, Phanerochaete chrysosporium PcGHR
rationale: GS-hydroquinone + GSH -> hydroquinone + GSSG is the defining reaction of the Xi-class glutathionyl-hydroquinone reductases, which work through a single catalytic cysteine and carry one activity. The MetaCyc entry names no protein, so enzyme assignment is from the chemistry.
direction_note: GSSG is missing from the products; the enzyme is a deglutathionylating reductase and does not run the glutathionylation of hydroquinone that ModelSEED's reverse direction implies.

enzyme_name: none identified (spontaneous lactonisation of the free acid; the catalysed route runs on the CoA thioester)
organism_context: Plant scopoletin/scopolin biosynthesis (Arabidopsis, tobacco)
rationale: Free (Z)-6'-hydroxyferulate lactonises to scopoletin without a catalyst; the enzymatic route in planta is the BAHD-family coumarin synthase COSY, which isomerises and lactonises the 6'-hydroxyferuloyl-CoA thioester, not the free acid. No protein is assigned to this free-acid step.
direction_note: The water released by lactonisation is missing (status MI:H:-1/O:-1|CI:1), so the dG estimate behind ModelSEED's reverse call was computed on an unbalanced equation; pathway flux runs toward the coumarin.

organism_context: Pseudomonas syringae pv. tabaci, MetaCyc PWY-7954
rationale: Tabtoxinine-beta-lactam is built from the lysine/DAP intermediate tetrahydrodipicolinate through several steps including acetylated intermediates and beta-lactam ring closure, so no single enzyme performs this conversion. The ModelSEED product formula (C7H11N2O4) is also not tabtoxinine-beta-lactam (C11H18N2O5) and the entry is mass-imbalanced (MI:H:4/N:1).
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux unambiguously runs tetrahydrodipicolinate -> toxin, but with several enzymes collapsed into one entry there is no single enzymology on which to base any direction bound.

organism_context: Fusarium fujikuroi / F. verticillioides fusarin gene cluster
rationale: The fusarin cluster deletion study assigns the carboxy-fusarin -> fusarin C methyl esterification to the stand-alone SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase FUS9, a single-domain MT with one activity. Identity rests on cluster genetics rather than a purified-enzyme assay, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way; the +27.7 kJ/mol dGPredictor value driving ModelSEED's reverse call has the wrong sign for this cofactor pair.

organism_context: Streptomyces rubellomurinus, FR-900098 / FR-33289 antibiotic pathway; homocitrate/citrate synthase family
rationale: FrbC is a citrate/homocitrate-synthase-family condensing enzyme that joins acetyl-CoA to 3-phosphonopyruvate at a single Claisen-condensation active site; it was characterised by heterologous expression of the frb cluster and shows no second activity.
direction_note: Acetyl-CoA condensations of this family are pulled irreversibly forward by hydrolysis of the thioester, so the retro-aldol/CoA-ligating direction ModelSEED assigns is not a physiological activity.

organism_context: E. coli / Pseudomonas stutzeri LldD (FMN, quinone-coupled); yeast flavocytochrome b2 (CYB2). In some bacteria the activity is the three-protein LutABC complex, which is a complex, not a fused multifunctional chain.
rationale: L-lactate oxidation to pyruvate at the expense of a flavin is done by FMN-dependent L-lactate dehydrogenases that pass electrons to quinone or cytochrome c; each is a single-activity flavoprotein. No enzyme is known that reduces pyruvate with free FADH2.
direction_note: Substituting free FAD/FADH2 (Em' about -219 mV) for enzyme-bound FMN plus the downstream quinone acceptor inverts the computed thermodynamics and is precisely why both eQuilibrator and dGPredictor, and hence ModelSEED, call this reaction reverse-only.

enzyme_name: hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:quinate hydroxycinnamoyl transferase (HQT/HCT, BAHD family), EC 2.3.1.99
organism_context: Plants: tomato and coffee HQT, poplar/Arabidopsis HCT
rationale: BAHD acyltransferases such as HQT/HCT transfer the hydroxycinnamoyl group from CoA to quinate in a single active site with no second catalytic activity. The 4-O-feruloyl regiochemistry is not pinned to a specific named protein, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: HCT/HQT are demonstrably reversible and the reverse direction (chlorogenate -> caffeoyl-CoA) carries real in-planta flux; all three dG estimates here sit within ~20 kJ/mol of zero, so neither a forward-only nor ModelSEED's reverse-only bound is justified.

organism_context: Thiobacillus thioparus THI115 and related sulfur-oxidising bacteria; cobalt-containing nitrile-hydratase relative
rationale: Thiocyanate + H2O -> carbonyl sulfide + ammonia is thiocyanate hydrolase; the enzyme is an (alpha-beta-gamma)4 assembly with one catalytic cobalt centre, and a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional under this protocol. Note ModelSEED names cpd32581 'isothiocyanate' but its formula and aliases (CNS-, thiocyanate ion) identify thiocyanate.
direction_note: Hydrolytic C-S/C-N cleavage releasing a gas (COS) is irreversible in vivo; no enzyme assembles thiocyanate from COS and ammonia.

organism_context: Anaerobic cobalamin pathway of Salmonella enterica and Bacillus megaterium
rationale: CbiD performs the single C-1 methylation converting cobalt-precorrin-5B to cobalt-precorrin-6A in the fully reconstituted anaerobic corrin pathway; it is a one-activity SAM methyltransferase with no second domain.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible; the +32.4 kJ/mol dGPredictor estimate behind ModelSEED's reverse call has the wrong sign for the SAM/SAH pair.

organism_context: Human and rat liver cytosolic SULTs; SULT1A1 and SULT1B1 dominate T4/T3 sulfation
rationale: Thyroxine sulfation is carried out by cytosolic SULTs, each a single-domain PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase with one catalytic activity. The Rhea entry names no isoform, so the specific protein is inferred from substrate preference.
direction_note: PAPS sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and one-way; running it in reverse would mean regenerating PAPS from PAP, which sulfotransferases do not do.

organism_context: Streptomyces albulus; streptothricin-resistance enzyme (ST non-producer)
rationale: SttH hydrolyses the amide bond of the streptolidine lactam of streptothricins, converting streptothricin D into streptothricin D acid and conferring resistance; the purified enzyme was shown to have this single hydrolytic activity.
direction_note: Lactam hydrolysis is irreversible; re-forming the streptolidine lactam would require ATP-dependent activation that this equation does not contain, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is not an enzymatic possibility.

distinct_activities: 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde dehydrogenase, NADP+-dependent (N-terminal ALDH domain), EC 1.2.1.91
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other bacteria carrying the paa phenylacetate catabolic pathway
rationale: PaaZ is one polypeptide carrying an N-terminal NADP+-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase domain and a C-terminal MaoC-like hydratase domain; the hydratase domain performs exactly the oxepin-CoA ring hydrolysis of this reaction. Cryo-EM shows both active sites on the same chain with substrate channelling between them.
direction_note: This is the clearest bifunctionality-explains-direction case in the chunk: the ALDH domain immediately and irreversibly oxidises the semialdehyde made by the hydratase domain, pulling the ring hydrolysis forward, so ModelSEED's reverse-only bound is wrong.

enzyme_name: none (futalosine pathway segment MqnA -> MqnE -> MqnB collapsed into one entry)
organism_context: Streptomyces, Helicobacter, Campylobacter, Thermus (futalosine route to menaquinone)
rationale: The three-substrate summary chorismate + inosine + PEP -> futalosine comes from the 2008 isotope-labelling study that defined the futalosine pathway, not from one enzyme; the real route runs MqnA (chorismate dehydratase), MqnE (radical-SAM aminofutalosine synthase) and MqnB (futalosine hydrolase). The entry is also mass-imbalanced, with C4H5O10P missing from the products.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux runs chorismate -> futalosine, but with three enzymes lumped there is no single enzymology on which to set a direction.

organism_context: Escherichia coli HPII; autocatalytic conversion of its own protoheme IX prosthetic group to heme d
rationale: HPII converts its own bound protoheme IX into cis-heme d using H2O2 during turnover, with heme d cis-diol as the intermediate; the catalyst is the catalase itself, which has one peroxide-utilising active site, so this is prosthetic-group self-processing and not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Oxidative heme maturation is a one-way event: heme d is never reduced back to protoheme plus hydrogen peroxide, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is not an enzymatic reaction.

organism_context: Fungi (Erg6) and plants/protists (SMT1/SMT2); this substrate pair, cholesta-5,7,24-trien-3beta-ol -> ergosta-5,7,24(28)-trien-3beta-ol, is the late-methylation branch of the ergosterol pathway
rationale: C-24 methylation of a Delta24 sterol with SAM is the single activity of sterol 24-C-methyltransferase; the substrate/product pair identifies the late-branch Erg6 reaction. Enzyme identity is inferred from chemistry and pathway position rather than an assay on these exact sterols.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-alkylation of an unactivated olefin is irreversible; the +43.9 kJ/mol dGPredictor value behind ModelSEED's reverse call has the wrong sign for the SAM/SAH pair.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana seed GAMT1/GAMT2 and angiosperm orthologues; GA deactivation by C-6 carboxyl methylation
rationale: SABATH-family GA methyltransferases carry one SAM-dependent carboxyl methyltransferase active site and no second activity; the GAMT clade is the only characterised catalyst of GA methyl-ester formation. Note that ModelSEED's substrate name 'GA41' is a naming artefact: the formula C19H23O5- and the product (O-methyl gibberellin A4) identify gibberellin A4.
direction_note: SAM-dependent carboxyl methyl esterification is strongly exergonic and one-way; this and the other four gibberellin methylations in this chunk all rest on the identical dGPredictor value of +29.04 +/- 16.56 kJ/mol, a single group-contribution number for the whole O-methylation class whose sign is wrong for a SAM/SAH couple.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana seed GAMT1/GAMT2 and angiosperm orthologues
rationale: Methylation of the C-6 carboxyl of gibberellin A1 to its methyl ester is the GAMT reaction; SABATH carboxyl methyltransferases are single-active-site enzymes with one catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH carboxyl methyl transfer is irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call comes from the same mis-signed +29.04 kJ/mol dGPredictor class estimate shared by all five gibberellin methylations here.
